scope: Additive exact-preimage patch and real production FAT host regression. Production files in this worktree and the primary checkout are unchanged by this handoff.
tested_behaviour: Existing regular-file replacement retains destination SFN alias, NT case byte and LFN slots.
Source unlink precedes target publication, including same-sector partial-write callbacks.
Old chain is freed after namespace writes, then all FAT copies and FSInfo synchronize.
Recoverable read/write/allocation failure preserves exact old destination after actual temporary-file removal and a fresh FAT mount.
No new data or directory-name slots needed for existing-target replacement, including full volumes.
Empty files, fragmented chains, maximum 255-unit source LFN, same/different directories, full/partial write errors, prohibited types and unchanged output on failure are exercised.
Validated acyclic chains share a suffix exactly when their terminal cluster IDs match; corrupt/shared input disables writes before caller cleanup.
Oversized source metadata with a shared suffix also disables writes before returning CORRUPT.
Persistent/torn rollback returns an error and disables further writes; raw outputs explicitly expose remaining orphan/mirror/FSInfo gaps.
